# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
A CONTROL THAT PROVES ITSELF IN A THROWAWAY DIRECTORY IS NOT PROVING ITSELF. The
doctor's fence check builds a fresh project, denies a foreign write there, deletes
it, and reports PASS. Every part of that is honest and the conclusion is still
wrong for this repository, because the fresh store it creates is one the installed
copy can read. The schema gap that broke the real fence cannot arise in the fixture.
Queued as M17.

A CONTROL THAT ANSWERS A NARROWER QUESTION THAN THE ONE YOU ASKED READS AS A PASS.
migrate_install.py checks whether a hook is WIRED. It printed NOTHING TO DO, it is
not stranded about an install whose hook allowed every write. Wiring was intact; the
code behind the wire was hundreds of commits stale. Queued as M18.

TWO FENCES GUARD THE SAME WRITE AND THE CHEAPER ONE ANSWERS FIRST. My first probe
of M15 got DENY on all three tracked paths and it would have been easy to report
"parked records are treated as live". The denials came from the battery fence
because a gate was running, not from ownership at all. The positive control is what
caught it: a deny whose REASON named a different mechanism than the one under test.
Read the reason, never only the verdict.

pgrep -f MATCHES THE SHELL THAT RUNS IT. Twice tonight `pgrep -f tools/test_all.py`,
the documented PO-4 check, returned a PID that was my own bash snapshot, because the
pattern text sat in my command line. Once it made me believe a gate was running when
none was. This is the same root as the recorded pkill incident, in read-only form:
confirm each PID with `ps -p <pid> -o command` before believing it.

AFTER A HISTORY REWRITE, A COMMIT COUNT IS NOT A MEASURE OF DIVERGENCE. 588 ahead
and 674 behind sounds like a fork. It was mostly the same work under new SHAs. What
actually mattered was the 13 subjects unique to one side, and three of those carried
client names. Compare subjects and content, never SHAs, and never trust a truncated
listing for a count.

A CASE-INSENSITIVE CLIENT SCAN MATCHES THE WORD hurry. The case-insensitive form
reported 12 hits on origin/main and 165 across tags. The documented case-sensitive
form reports 0. Every one of the 12 was the English word "hurry", several of them
test fixtures that deliberately keep the word as proof the scan does not over-match.
I nearly reported a public leak that does not exist.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
